name: entry_and_tables
title: Entry jump, move tables, scene map pointers, high scores, score values and mode texts

comments.text: Program entry from the loader. It jumps to the cold start at $1601.
Move table, one byte per move $00-$18. Bit 7 keeps the input of the move; nonzero lets the move return to the stance by itself.
Move table: 1 for the 11 attack moves ($06, $07, $0a-$11, $18).
Move table: the block or dodge that answers each attack move, 0 for none.
Move table of 21 bytes: reach type of the attack. Moves $15-$18 read the first 4 bytes of the next table, which are 0.
Move table: reach value for a full point of the attack.
Move table: reach value for a half point of the attack.
Table of 21 bytes with 1 for moves $07, $0a, $0b, $0c and $11. No instruction indexes it; a read with a large index reaches $11ed and $11f4.
Move table: the shape frame of the attack that does the hit test.
Move table of words: hit zone table of the attack when the fighters face each other, 0 for no attack.
Move table of words: hit zone table of the attack when both fighters face the same way.
Unused old table of 4 words: $e640, $3600, $4500, $5400. These are unpacked scene bitmaps of $f00 bytes; scene 0 sat at its screen place.
Colour map of each scene (480 bytes each), copied to colour RAM rows 5-16 by scene_copy_maps.
Screen map of each scene (480 bytes each), the bitmap colours of rows 5-16.
High score of the one-player game: six characters, leading spaces. high_score_update writes it.
High score of the two-player game: six characters, leading spaces.
Move table: points of a full-point hit in hundreds. A half point gives half.
Mode text at the bottom right of the panel. The panel character set has ASCII order.
Screen offset of the yin-yang symbols of fighter 0 and fighter 1.
